LESSON: WRITING 5.3.2 WRITING SYLLABLES (JA-JU, LA-LU)

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Writing 5.3.2 Writing syllables (ja-ju, la-lu)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 5.3.2 Writing syllables (ja-ju, la-lu), part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: How do we sit when writing? 2. Which tools do we use for writing syllables?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 5.3.2 Writing syllables (ja-ju, la-lu) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: connecting using technology skill as learner writes syllables on ICT devices.

● Self-efficacy as learner displays assertively work done on syllables.

Values:
● Respect: acceptance as learner with in harmony with others.

● Responsibility: self drive as learner writes syllables without assistance.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Social cohesion as learner interacts with others in activities while writing syllables and even as they share writing tools.

Link to other Activity Areas:

environmental activities as learner make patterns using syllables and letter sounds to form names of animals found within
